layout: TRAIN AND EVAL SHIPPED AS SEPARATE FILES — the split is the data layout, not a manifest a trainer must apply
changes_from_v7.1: the 6 deployed-val40 clips ADDED to eval (they already carried full v7.1 labels; they were held out of training and previously unused)
every clip now assigned — nothing discarded

deployed_val40_overlap.consequence: ⛔ NOT a leak — neither set is trained on, and the TRAIN cache is asserted val40-clean by digest (0 of 4,713). But the overlap is now REAL: our eval and val40 share 6 clips (15% of val40, 4% of our eval). ⚠️ AND THOSE 6 ARE val40's ONLY LABELLED CLIPS (34 of its 40 carry no v7 labels), so ANY LABEL-BASED comparison between our eval and val40 would share its ENTIRE support. State it whenever the two are compared.
deployed_val40_overlap.became_live_when: the 6 clips gained epcache episodes. Until then they carried labels but NO pixels, contributed nothing to a val round, and the overlap was nominal — our eval curve and THE published val40 statistic were still effectively independent.

episode_cache.why_separate: two directories is a STRUCTURAL guarantee that the train cache is val40-clean; one directory with a filter is only a promise. Verified after the build: train cache byte-identical (4,713 episodes, 177,998,547,213 bytes, same _geometry.json hash), caches disjoint, train val40 members = 0.

interpretation.admissible_use: aggregate val curve at any cadence; checkpoint selection.
interpretation.inadmissible_use: ⛔ PER-COMPETENCE numbers — at n=147 the eval side holds only ~13 stop-launch and ~24 highway clips. Also not a substitute for the deployed val40, which it now partially overlaps.
